areas: Complete scenes you can play with the keyboard.
Scripts, physics, prefabs, includes and scene transitions.
Sprites, tiles, 2D lights, particles and custom passes.
Imported models, skinning, textures and material variants.
Light types, shadow maps and contact, blob and darkness shading.
Camera backgrounds, procedural and physical skies, HDR range.
Water, gems, character, pickup and animated effect materials.
Fog, depth of field and the scenes the post-effect checks drive.
Seeded particle bursts in 3D and display space.
Invalid content that must stop with a clear diagnostic.

FoxShowcase.title: Fox sunset world
FoxShowcase.summary: A third-person sunset valley with an animated explorer, roaming wildlife, dense wind-swept grass, forests, mountains, a beach and an illustrated field journal.
FoxShowcase.lookFor: WASD walks, Shift moves briskly and Space jumps; drag orbits and the wheel zooms. Follow the trails and press E near five field-note sites. The journal has an illustrated map and real pointer/keyboard UI controls. F and G operate the sanctuary relic.

EmberRun.title: Ember Run
EmberRun.summary: A small 2D platformer built entirely from authored scenes and scripts.
EmberRun.lookFor: Select Play, click the game, then move with WASD or the arrows, dash with Space and retry with R. Collect amber embers and dodge red hazards.

ReferenceStart.title: Gameplay reference
ReferenceStart.summary: The Rust gameplay reference: a player, a spawned pickup, a score counter, audio and a save, then a scene change to the result screen.
ReferenceStart.lookFor: Hold Space to score; the score text updates and the run saves. After a second the game switches to the result scene. The gameplay parity harness compares this scene tick by tick with native.

ReferenceResult.title: Gameplay reference result
ReferenceResult.summary: The result screen the gameplay reference loads after its countdown.
ReferenceResult.lookFor: Normally reached from Gameplay reference; opened directly it shows the final score text.

default.title: Reference project default
default.lookFor: A minimal scene confirming the project boots.

BrowserDependencies.title: Includes and prefabs
BrowserDependencies.summary: A scene built from an included scene fragment plus prefab instances with additions, removals and overrides.
BrowserDependencies.lookFor: All included and prefab-instanced models appear with their overridden materials and positions.

BrowserIncluded.title: Included fragment
BrowserIncluded.summary: The scene fragment that Includes and prefabs pulls in.
BrowserIncluded.lookFor: Open Includes and prefabs to see it composed into a full scene.

BrowserPhysics3D.title: 3D physics and joints
BrowserPhysics3D.summary: Jolt 3D physics running in the browser with the same deterministic engine code as native: a box falls onto a static floor, a pendulum swings on a hinge joint, and a second box is welded to the falling one with a fixed joint.
BrowserPhysics3D.lookFor: Select Play: the box lands and settles with its welded partner, and the pendulum swings. At tick 60 the falling box sits at (-0.01254, 0.52681, 0.01704) on both native and browser.

BrowserBodies3D.title: 3D bodies: velocity, force and impulse
BrowserBodies3D.summary: A script sets velocity on one box, pushes another with a force for 20 ticks and kicks a third with an impulse, next to a hinge pendulum and a fixed-joint pair; the script publishes the velocities it reads back. The same Rust or C# probe runs natively and in the browser.
BrowserBodies3D.lookFor: Select Play: the slider skids to a stop, the pusher shoves along +X and the kicked box hops while its welded partner follows.

BrowserRaycast3D.title: 3D raycasts
BrowserRaycast3D.summary: A script casts rays at a floor, a wall, a sphere, a 45-degree rotated box, an oblique ray and a falling box, and publishes each distance, point, normal and whether the right entity was hit.
BrowserRaycast3D.lookFor: Select Play: the dropper falls beside the targets. The probe's published hit distances and normals match the native run to 1e-5.

BrowserContacts3D.title: 3D collision and trigger events
BrowserContacts3D.summary: A bouncing box produces repeated collision enter/exit events and a box dropped through a static sensor volume produces one trigger enter and exit; every body counts its own events in published script properties.
BrowserContacts3D.lookFor: Select Play: the left box bounces to rest while the right box falls through the invisible sensor zone and lands.

BrowserCharacter3D.title: 3D character controller
BrowserCharacter3D.summary: A character controller walks with the arrow keys, steps onto a low platform, jumps with space and shoves a crate; the probe publishes grounded state, jump count and peak height.
BrowserCharacter3D.lookFor: Hold Right to walk onto the step and into the crate, tap Space to jump, and hold Up to walk away from the camera.

BrowserRagdoll3D.title: 3D ragdoll from the Human skeleton
BrowserRagdoll3D.summary: A script spawns a physics ragdoll from the Human skeleton at tick 0; the bone bodies and their joints collapse onto the floor, and every bone's world transform is compared with the native run.
BrowserRagdoll3D.lookFor: Select Play: capsule bones fall into a heap on the floor in the same arrangement natively and in the browser.

BrowserSkinClips3D.title: 3D skinned clip control
BrowserSkinClips3D.summary: A script switches the Human's skinned clips outright, cross-fades between them and changes the playback speed, publishing the live clip index and clip time each tick.
BrowserSkinClips3D.lookFor: Select Play: the Human plays the first clip, switches to Walk, cross-fades back, then speeds up and slows down.

BrowserPrefab3D.title: Scripted 3D prefab instances
BrowserPrefab3D.summary: A script instantiates a crate prefab and a barrel prefab, places them, destroys the crate and instantiates a second crate; each prefab is a physics body, the crate with a child mesh.
BrowserPrefab3D.lookFor: Select Play: a crate drops in, then a barrel; the crate disappears and a new one drops in at the centre.

BrowserTransition3D.title: 3D scene transition
BrowserTransition3D.summary: A box falls for 20 ticks, the script writes a save and loads a second 3D scene with its own bodies and script, which reads the save back.
BrowserTransition3D.lookFor: Select Play: after a third of a second the scene switches to a platform where a sphere bounces.

BrowserTransition3DResult.title: 3D transition destination
BrowserTransition3DResult.summary: The second 3D scene that 3D scene transition loads.
BrowserTransition3DResult.lookFor: Open 3D scene transition to see it entered after 20 ticks.

BrowserFeatures.title: 2D features
BrowserFeatures.summary: Tilemaps, sprite animation, text and UI widgets in one 2D scene.
BrowserFeatures.lookFor: Animated sprites play, tiles align on the grid and UI text is crisp and correctly ordered.

BrowserFontParity.title: Analytic font curves
BrowserFontParity.summary: Roboto text and a project-local Font Awesome icon font exercise native and browser text rendering.
BrowserFontParity.lookFor: Compare the wrapped and aligned labels and the three custom-font icons against the native capture.

BrowserUiParity.title: Scene UI widgets and clipping
BrowserUiParity.summary: Rounded controls, text boxes and nested masks over a 3D camera background.
BrowserUiParity.lookFor: Compare the rounded widget corners and the nested red, green and blue clipped regions. Click the text fields to enter and select text.

BrowserUiShaders.title: Scene UI effects and materials
BrowserUiShaders.summary: Background and overlay UI effects and a per-element material, paired with an unshaded control.
BrowserUiShaders.lookFor: The feature scene colours three rectangular regions; the control omits the custom shaders.

BrowserLight2D.title: 2D lighting
BrowserLight2D.summary: A 2D lamp casting shadows through a tile artwork silhouette, using the native light-map equations.
BrowserLight2D.lookFor: Shadows follow the tile art's alpha edges, not its rectangle.

BrowserParticles2D.title: 2D particles
BrowserParticles2D.lookFor: Particles spawn from the emitter and fade the same way every load.

BrowserCustomPass.title: Custom render passes
BrowserCustomPass.summary: A Rust script submits project custom passes (behind, over and emissive) through the portable CustomPass.slangh shader contract.
BrowserCustomPass.lookFor: The behind rectangle is hidden by the sprite, the over rectangle is lit like the sprite, and both emissive rectangles stay fully bright. The control scene turns the passes off.

BrowserModels.title: Models
BrowserModels.summary: Authored multi-primitive glTF models with linked materials and depth testing.
BrowserModels.lookFor: Overlapping models sort by depth regardless of draw order.

BrowserMaterials.title: Material textures
BrowserMaterials.summary: Texture colour spaces, mipmaps, alpha transparency and face culling.
BrowserMaterials.lookFor: Distant surfaces use smaller mips without shimmering; cutout and blended alpha edges are clean.

BrowserSkin.title: Skinned animation
BrowserSkin.summary: Skinned models playing animation clips with the shared pose evaluator.
BrowserSkin.lookFor: Characters animate smoothly with no detached limbs.

BrowserPbrMaps.title: PBR texture maps
BrowserPbrMaps.summary: Tangent-space normals, ambient occlusion and metallic/roughness maps.
BrowserPbrMaps.lookFor: Surface detail catches the light from the normal map; rough and metallic regions differ.

BrowserSampler.title: Texture sampling
BrowserSampler.summary: Front-facing and grazing-angle striped cards for anisotropy and mip LOD bias comparisons.
BrowserSampler.lookFor: The qualification runner varies texture filtering settings over the same geometry.

BrowserSpecularVariance.title: Normal-map specular filtering
BrowserSpecularVariance.summary: A minified high-frequency normal map on a smooth metallic card.
BrowserSpecularVariance.lookFor: Compare specularFilter disabled and enabled with identical camera and lighting.

BrowserDataMipAlpha.title: Data texture mip alpha independence
BrowserDataMipAlpha.summary: A minified metallic-roughness texture whose unused alpha varies while its data channels match the opaque control.
BrowserDataMipAlpha.lookFor: The highlight should remain unchanged between the two scenes.

BrowserCrossMirror.title: Mirrored blended tangent normals
BrowserCrossMirror.summary: A nonuniform reflected, alpha-blended card with a tangent-space normal map.
BrowserCrossMirror.lookFor: The reflection reverses the normal-map light response relative to the control.

BrowserCrossMaskOn.title: Mirrored cutout shadows
BrowserCrossMaskOn.summary: A mirrored, nonuniform alpha-cutout caster over a shadow receiver.
BrowserCrossMaskOn.lookFor: The opaque portion casts while the cutout remains lit; the solid control casts into the hole.

BrowserCrossMaskSolid.title: Solid caster control
BrowserCrossMaskSolid.summary: The same caster without its cutout.
BrowserCrossMaskSolid.lookFor: The solid caster fills the cutout's shadow.

BrowserCrossSkinOn.title: Animated mirrored cutout skin
BrowserCrossSkinOn.summary: A moving skinned, mirrored and nonuniform cutout shadow caster.
BrowserCrossSkinOn.lookFor: The shadow follows the animated silhouette.

BrowserVertexColor.title: Vertex colours
BrowserVertexColor.summary: A card whose corners carry red, green, blue and yellow vertex colours with modulateVertexColor enabled.
BrowserVertexColor.lookFor: Each corner takes its vertex hue. The control ignores vertex colours and stays uniform.

BrowserUvScroll.title: UV scrolling
BrowserUvScroll.summary: A four-band stripe texture scrolled by the material's uv_scroll.
BrowserUvScroll.lookFor: The stripes move; by tick 10 they have shifted by exactly one band. The control has zero scroll.

BrowserGraph.title: Material graph
BrowserGraph.summary: A material-graph shader lowered to WGSL by the shared graph compiler.
BrowserGraph.lookFor: The graph material renders the same pattern as native.

BrowserGraphBackface.title: Material graph backfaces
BrowserGraphBackface.summary: A double-sided material-graph surface seen from behind.
BrowserGraphBackface.lookFor: The back face renders with the graph's backface output; the control culls it.

BrowserBaked.title: Baked lighting
BrowserBaked.summary: Prelit vertex colours that keep their bake, with cascade shadows only darkening.
BrowserBaked.lookFor: Baked shading stays put; real-time shadows darken it but never brighten it.

BrowserFoliage.title: Foliage wind
BrowserFoliage.summary: Alpha-masked, baked foliage swaying in world-space wind, including its shadows.
BrowserFoliage.lookFor: Leaves and their shadows move together; the control is still.

BrowserSun.title: Sunlight
BrowserSun.summary: Directional sunlight on a rough dielectric surface.
BrowserSun.lookFor: Even lighting with a soft specular response.

BrowserPoint.title: Point light
BrowserPoint.summary: A point light with native inverse-square attenuation.
BrowserPoint.lookFor: Brightness falls off with distance from the light.

BrowserSpot.title: Spotlight
BrowserSpot.summary: Spotlight cone falloff on an authored surface.
BrowserSpot.lookFor: A clear cone with a soft edge.

BrowserTileOrthoOn.title: Orthographic tiled-light capacity
BrowserTileOrthoOn.summary: 129 distributed point lights and an off-axis target.
BrowserTileOrthoOn.lookFor: The target adds a warm patch to the receiver.

BrowserTilePerspectiveOn.title: Perspective tiled-light capacity
BrowserTilePerspectiveOn.summary: 129 distributed point lights and an off-axis target.
BrowserTilePerspectiveOn.lookFor: The target adds a warm patch to the receiver.

BrowserShadowBudgetSelected.title: Point shadow entry budget
BrowserShadowBudgetSelected.summary: An eighth selected point shadow consumes the last six atlas entries.
BrowserShadowBudgetSelected.lookFor: The receiver shadow disappears in the nine-point control.

BrowserShadowAtlas17On.title: Seventeen local shadow maps
BrowserShadowAtlas17On.summary: A visible spot shadow follows sixteen other atlas maps.
BrowserShadowAtlas17On.lookFor: The receiver shadow disappears in the control.

BrowserShadowFarFadeOn.title: Directional shadow far fade
BrowserShadowFarFadeOn.summary: Three receivers straddle the directional shadow fade and distance cutoff.
BrowserShadowFarFadeOn.lookFor: Compare the three shadows against the unshadowed control.

BrowserDefaultLighting.title: Default lighting
BrowserDefaultLighting.summary: A 3D scene with no authored lights, using the engine's default sun and ambient.
BrowserDefaultLighting.lookFor: Models are lit even though the scene defines no lights.

BrowserObjectLights.title: Object lights
BrowserObjectLights.summary: Ambient plus two native object light records on objectLit materials.
BrowserObjectLights.lookFor: The object picks up both coloured lights; the control shows ambient only.

BrowserShadowSunOn.title: Sun shadows
BrowserShadowSunOn.summary: Directional cascade shadows on a receiver.
BrowserShadowSunOn.lookFor: A crisp shadow under the caster; the control disables receiving.

BrowserShadowPointOn.title: Point light shadows
BrowserShadowPointOn.summary: Point light shadows from the local shadow atlas.
BrowserShadowPointOn.lookFor: An asymmetric shadow pointing away from the light; the control disables receiving.

BrowserShadowSpotOn.title: Spotlight shadows
BrowserShadowSpotOn.summary: Spotlight shadows from the local shadow atlas.
BrowserShadowSpotOn.lookFor: The shadow sits inside the cone; the control disables receiving.

BrowserShadowMaskOn.title: Alpha-cutout shadows
BrowserShadowMaskOn.lookFor: The shadow has the cutout holes, not a solid quad.

BrowserShadowSkinOn.title: Skinned-model shadows
BrowserShadowSkinOn.summary: Shadows from an animated skinned model.
BrowserShadowSkinOn.lookFor: The shadow follows the animated pose.

BrowserShadowNoCast.title: Non-casting mesh
BrowserShadowNoCast.summary: An alpha-cutout mesh that stays visible while its shadow-casting flag is off.
BrowserShadowNoCast.lookFor: The mesh is drawn but leaves no shadow.

BrowserContact.title: Contact shadows
BrowserContact.summary: Screen-space contact shadows where objects meet the ground.
BrowserContact.lookFor: A thin dark contact line under each object.

BrowserBlob.title: Blob shadows
BrowserBlob.summary: Object blob shadows built from cooked model bounds.
BrowserBlob.lookFor: A soft blob under each object, sized to its bounds.

BrowserDarkness.title: Darkness volumes
BrowserDarkness.summary: Authored darkness volumes that dim everything inside them.
BrowserDarkness.lookFor: The region inside the volume is darker; the control has no volume.

BrowserSolid.title: Solid background
BrowserSolid.summary: A camera solid colour preserved through the HDR compositor.
BrowserSolid.lookFor: The exact authored colour, with no tonemap shift.

BrowserGradient.title: Gradient background
BrowserGradient.summary: Camera colour stops blended in display space.
BrowserGradient.lookFor: A smooth gradient with no banding steps.

BrowserSky.title: Procedural sky
BrowserSky.summary: The native procedural sky gradient with horizon and ground colours.
BrowserSky.lookFor: A bright horizon band between sky and ground colours.

BrowserPhysicalSky.title: Physical sky
BrowserPhysicalSky.summary: Atmospheric scattering with a sun, using the shared sky math.
BrowserPhysicalSky.lookFor: A blue zenith fading to a warm horizon around the sun.

BrowserClouds.title: Clouds
BrowserClouds.summary: Procedural cloud layer over the sky.
BrowserClouds.lookFor: Soft clouds across the sky; the control is clear.

BrowserSkyMesh.title: Sky dome mesh
BrowserSkyMesh.summary: An authored dome mesh marked as sky, drawn behind everything without writing depth.
BrowserSkyMesh.lookFor: The cube stays in front even though the dome is nearer. In the control the dome is ordinary geometry and hides the cube.

BrowserHdr.title: HDR range
BrowserHdr.summary: Half and eight units of scene radiance through native ACES tonemapping.
BrowserHdr.lookFor: The bright patch rolls off smoothly instead of clipping.

BrowserWater.title: Water
BrowserWater.summary: Shared ripple shading, screen reflections, sun glints and depth tint.
BrowserWater.lookFor: Rippling reflections and glints; the control is a plain surface.

BrowserWaterDeep.title: Deep water tint
BrowserWaterDeep.summary: The water scene with a deep seabed, to check depth-based tint.
BrowserWaterDeep.lookFor: Compared with Water, the water reads darker and more saturated.

BrowserGem.title: Gem
BrowserGem.summary: Facet normals, fresnel rim, fake interior refraction and sparkle.
BrowserGem.lookFor: Bright facet edges and sparkle; the control is a plain material.

BrowserSheen.title: Pickup sheen
BrowserSheen.summary: Collectible sheen: an object-lit rim and moving highlight.
BrowserSheen.lookFor: A glossy rim highlight on the pickup.

BrowserCharacter.title: Character lighting
BrowserCharacter.summary: Wrapped key light, rim light, eye catchlight and blob contact for characters.
BrowserCharacter.lookFor: Softer wrapped shading and a rim outline; the control uses standard shading.

BrowserPlasma.title: Plasma effect
BrowserPlasma.summary: The built-in animated plasma effect material.
BrowserPlasma.lookFor: Animated plasma bands; the control has zero intensity.

BrowserMolten.title: Molten effect
BrowserMolten.summary: The built-in molten effect, whose noise is bit-identical across backends.
BrowserMolten.lookFor: Glowing molten cracks; the control has zero intensity.

BrowserLightShaft.title: Light shaft cards
BrowserLightShaft.summary: Blended light shaft cards with shimmer and soft depth intersection.
BrowserLightShaft.lookFor: Soft shafts that fade where they meet geometry.

BrowserFog.title: Height fog
BrowserFog.summary: Height and distance fog over the scene.
BrowserFog.lookFor: Distant and low geometry fades into the fog colour.

BrowserDofOn.title: Depth of field
BrowserDofOn.summary: Thin-lens depth of field from the camera's lens settings.
BrowserDofOn.lookFor: The focus plane is sharp; near and far objects blur.

BrowserPostPattern.title: Post-effect test pattern
BrowserPostPattern.summary: Mid-grey, warm and cool radiance, a tiny HDR highlight and fine diagonals. The post checks switch grading, vignette, chromatic aberration, grain, bloom, FXAA, sharpening and render scale on over it.
BrowserPostPattern.lookFor: Opened here it shows the neutral pattern; effects come from graphics settings.

BrowserPostCorner.title: Post-effect corner
BrowserPostCorner.summary: A warm and a cool cube in a corner on a reflective floor, used for GTAO, SSR, volumetrics and their sweeps.
BrowserPostCorner.lookFor: Neutral layout; the post checks enable ambient occlusion and reflections over it.

BrowserPostVolumetric.title: Volumetric air
BrowserPostVolumetric.summary: A participating-air layout for volumetric fog scattering.
BrowserPostVolumetric.lookFor: Neutral layout; the post checks enable volumetrics over it.

BrowserPostDisplay.title: Display-space particles
BrowserPostDisplay.summary: Particles drawn after tonemapping, used for FXAA, sharpening and render-scale checks.
BrowserPostDisplay.lookFor: Particles sit on top of the tonemapped scene.

BrowserPostExposure.title: Auto exposure meter
BrowserPostExposure.summary: A frame filled with exactly HDR 2 radiance so auto exposure can be checked against an analytic meter.
BrowserPostExposure.lookFor: Neutral layout; with auto exposure on, brightness adapts over the first frames.

BrowserPostMotion.title: Camera motion
BrowserPostMotion.summary: A Rust-scripted moving camera used for motion blur.
BrowserPostMotion.lookFor: Select Play: the camera pans. Motion blur is enabled by the post checks.

BrowserPostTemporalCut.title: Temporal camera cut
BrowserPostTemporalCut.summary: A camera cut on the tenth fixed update for temporal history probes.
BrowserPostTemporalCut.lookFor: The camera changes position during play.

BrowserPostTemporalSwitch.title: Temporal scene switch
BrowserPostTemporalSwitch.summary: A scene switch on the tenth fixed update for temporal history probes.

BrowserPostTemporalControl.title: Temporal history control
BrowserPostTemporalControl.summary: A stationary camera control for temporal history probes.

BrowserPostTemporalDestination.title: Temporal switch destination
BrowserPostTemporalDestination.summary: The destination camera pose for the temporal scene switch.
BrowserPostTemporalDestination.lookFor: The camera starts at the destination pose.

BrowserPostTonemap.title: Tonemap bands
BrowserPostTonemap.summary: Eight neutral radiance bands for checking all eleven tonemap operators.
BrowserPostTonemap.lookFor: Eight grey steps from dark to bright.

BrowserParticles3D.title: 3D particles
BrowserParticles3D.summary: A fixed-seed 3D particle burst with depth.
BrowserParticles3D.lookFor: Particles pass behind and in front of geometry correctly.

BrowserParticlesDisplayOnly.title: Display-only particles
BrowserParticlesDisplayOnly.summary: A particle burst drawn only in display space.
BrowserParticlesDisplayOnly.lookFor: Particles render over the scene without scene lighting.

BrowserBadAtlas.title: Invalid sprite atlas
BrowserBadAtlas.summary: A sprite atlas whose regions are invalid.
BrowserBadAtlas.lookFor: Loading stops with an atlas diagnostic.

BrowserBadAudio.title: Invalid audio
BrowserBadAudio.summary: An audio asset the browser cannot decode.
BrowserBadAudio.lookFor: Loading stops with an audio diagnostic.

BrowserBadFont.title: Invalid font
BrowserBadFont.summary: A font asset that fails validation.
BrowserBadFont.lookFor: Loading stops with a font diagnostic.

BrowserBadLight.title: NaN light
BrowserBadLight.summary: A light with a NaN value.
BrowserBadLight.lookFor: The frame is rejected before GPU submission, with a diagnostic.

BrowserBadParticleCapacity.title: Particle capacity
BrowserBadParticleCapacity.summary: An emitter that asks for more particles than the budget allows.
BrowserBadParticleCapacity.lookFor: Rejected with a particle budget diagnostic.

BrowserBadParticleRate.title: Particle rate
BrowserBadParticleRate.summary: An emitter with an invalid spawn rate.

BrowserBadVersion.title: Unsupported scene version
BrowserBadVersion.summary: A scene file with a version the runtime does not accept.
BrowserBadVersion.lookFor: Loading stops with a version diagnostic.

BrowserBadCustomPassShader.title: Missing custom pass shader
BrowserBadCustomPassShader.summary: A script registers a custom pass with an unknown shader.
BrowserBadCustomPassShader.lookFor: Fails with WEB_CUSTOM_PASS_SHADER before any custom pass is drawn.

BrowserBadCustomPassBudget.title: Custom pass budget
BrowserBadCustomPassBudget.summary: A script submits 69,632 float4s against the 65,536 per-frame budget.
BrowserBadCustomPassBudget.lookFor: Fails with WEB_CUSTOM_PASS_BUDGET before GPU submission.
